$comment: W0 — the Workbench's first-paint verb set, and the budget W3 has to bring it inside. Machine-readable so scripts/perf/workbench-load.mjs can replay exactly this burst against a live plane, and so workbench/tests/firstPaintBudget.spec.ts can assert the call count and transfer size against the same source of truth instead of a number typed twice.
capturedFrom: static trace of every TanStack query mounted on a cold load of the deployed build (cms-agent.netlify.app/workbench/), cross-checked against the operator's browser waterfall of the same date (15 verbs). Re-derive with: grep the hooks mounted by App.tsx's always-on subtree plus the active screen.

budget.appliesTo: everything issued before the rail is interactive
budget.rationale: Design decision 3 of the runner plan. A verb whose p95 exceeds 3s gets a projection or an index, never a longer timeout.

calls.why: ⌘K's node index. The palette is mounted for the app's whole lifetime (App.tsx) and this query is not gated on paletteOpen, so every cold load pays the flat 48-node workspace list whether or not the palette is ever opened.
calls.note: 310 KB; prompt 53%, outputSchema 17%, deprecated `schema` alias 12% (38 KB pure duplicate)

calls.origin: components/CommandPalette.tsx:189 + components/StartRunModal.tsx:50 useProjects() (one network call, two observers)
calls.why: Project picker options. Genuinely needed on first paint — the only one of the palette's three that survives the budget.
Node COUNT for the workflow menu. Downloads a whole graph to read `.nodes.length`.
Same, third catalog workflow. The catalog lists 3; the live registry has 6, so this fan-out grows with the registry.
The rail's real topology. Distinct query key from workflowCountsQ's identical call — the same graph is fetched twice on one paint.
Recent runs for the rail's run chips.
Per-node score glyphs. Nothing above the fold needs it — leaves first paint in W3.
"Learned since your last visit" badges. Degrades to no badges on failure — must not be on the critical path.
Inspector header. Seeded from the ['nodes'] cache, so this is a background refresh — but it is still a request in the burst.
Default inspector tab is `prompt`, so this fires on every cold load.
Learned prompt material for the same tab.
Skill names for the prompt's skill chips. The whole skill catalogue, for a chip row.
Fires when the operator's persisted tab is `default` rather than `prompt` — one of the two tab-dependent members of the burst.
W3 — registeredWorkflowIds + summary graph + 5 summary run rows + attention counts + workspaceVersion, all from W1's cached reads.
Project picker options; small, and needed by the run-start path the operator reaches first.

movedOffFirstPaint.to: served from bootstrap; TopBar reads counts off the summary graph instead of fetching one graph per workflow

after.verifiedBy: workbench/tests/firstPaintBudget.spec.ts — asserts this file's budget against window.__verbCalls (api/client.ts) filtered to calls started strictly before window.__railInteractiveAt (Rail.tsx). Both seams are DEV-only.

boundaryCases.note: Issued in the SAME React commit the rail becomes interactive in: the rail adopts a first node, and the inspector reads it. It is a consequence of first paint, not a precondition for it, so it is outside the budget by the strict-inequality rule in the spec — but it is still one call for one node, not a 310 KB list.
